The immigration authority shared the reminder on X (formerly Twitter), also making clear that changing an address with the US Postal Service does not automatically update records with USCIS.“Changing your address with USPS does not update your address with USCIS, and USPS will not forward USCIS mail. You are responsible for keeping your address current with both USCIS and USPS. If you do not update your address with USCIS, you may miss notices, your case may be delayed, and you may not receive your immigration documents,” the agency wrote.The post also has a link to the USCIS webpage detailing the process of address change. Here’s what it saysIf you have filed an immigration benefit request with USCIS, you must notify USCIS of any changes of address as soon as possible to ensure you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Additionally, all aliens in the United States must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving. This reporting requirement does not apply to A and G visa holders and visa waiver visitors.We strongly encourage you to submit your change of address through a USCIS online account as soon as you move.Changing your address with the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) will not change your address with USCIS and USPS will not forward your mail from USCIS. Please update your information with both USCIS and USPS. We recommend you use the USPS Look Up a ZIP Code tool to ensure that you give USCIS your full address using the standard abbreviations and formatting recognized by USPS.Using an online account to update your address in a timely way meets the legal requirement to notify us that you have moved. It also ensures that your case will continue processing without interruption and that you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Changing your address online allows us to process your change of address almost immediately and eliminates the need to file a paper Form AR-11, Alien’s Change of Address Card, by mail.Most people can change their address online using the USCIS Enterprise Change of Address (E-COA) self-service change-of-address tool. This tool can be found in their USCIS Online Account under the My Account dropdown menu. If you do not have a USCIS online account, see our How to Create a USCIS Online Account page. Some people may not have access to this feature, see the Specific Procedures for Certain Populations section for more information.If you have a pending, approved, or previously filed case with USCIS, you may change your address using your USCIS online account even if you initially filed your benefit request by mail.NOTE: If you use your USCIS online account to change your address, you must enter the receipt numbers for each pending benefit request to apply the address change. Providing receipt numbers helps ensure that we update your address where needed and that you continue to receive important correspondence and benefits related to these cases from USCIS without delay.You also may file a paper Form AR-11 by mail to change your address. This meets the legal requirement to notify USCIS of a change of address. However, because filing a paper-based Form AR-11 does not provide for an automated update to your address in USCIS systems, we strongly encourage requestors to use the self-service change of address tool available in their USCIS online account when reporting a change of address.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has a reminder for immigrants in the country asking them to report a change of address to the agency within 10 days of moving. The immigration authority shared the reminder on X (formerly Twitter) changing an address with the US Postal Service does not automatically update records with USCIS.

Article Title: Google engineer quits his "amazing" job over AI, and says the doomers have it wrong: I am not convinced the chance of ASI doom is…
Article Text:
Google DeepMind engineer says his chip design work was speeding up AI

This AI safety resignation stops short of predicting doom

O'Callahan plans to keep working on AI after leaving Google

Poll Vote & Share your view Is it ethical for AI engineers to prioritize making AI cheaper and faster over potential risks? Yes, that's their goal No, ethics should come first 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Robert O'Callahan, a Google DeepMind engineer based in Auckland, has resigned over how fast artificial intelligence is advancing. In a resignation email shared on his blog this week, he wrote that AI progress is "far too rapid". His team's goal of making AI "much cheaper and lower-latency", he added, was not good for people right now.Yet O'Callahan stops short of the extinction warnings that have dominated the AI debate this month. He wrote that he is "not convinced the chance of ASI doom is 100%", referring to artificial superintelligence. The risk, in his view, is "real but uncertain". That alone, he argued, makes chasing ASI in the near future "inherently irresponsible".O'Callahan did not build AI models himself. He worked on tools for hardware chip design. For a while, he wrote, he told himself the work was relatively harmless. Over time he came to accept that its main impact would be faster design of a new breed of AI chips, making AI cheaper, faster and more capable.His exit lands in the same week Google laid out plans to test its AI chips in space. Under Project Suncatcher, a prototype satellite carrying Google's Trillium TPUs will fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission.The satellite was built with Earth imaging company Planet. The long-term goal is to see whether orbit could host AI data centres, since solar panels there can generate up to eight times more power than on Earth. "One small step for TPUs...," CEO Sundar Pichai posted on X. O'Callahan's post does not mention the project.Leaving was not easy. He said being "paid handsomely to solve fun puzzles" had been amazing. Moving teams was impractical too, since Google has no other engineering teams in New Zealand. A Christian and a church elder in Auckland, he wrote that ignoring his work's impact "would not be a Jesus-following thing to do".He joins a string of researchers who have left top AI labs over safety fears. Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic earlier this month, later warning in an interview that "we could all die" if development did not slow down. Former Google DeepMind researchers Rishub Jain and Bilal Chughtai also left this year.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has since proposed slowing frontier AI development, with Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk backing him publicly. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back, calling extinction warnings "doomsday narratives".O'Callahan sits somewhere between the two camps. He wrote that several doomer predictions, including reward hacking, misalignment and deceptive models, have already come true. But he has seen no hard evidence that insiders are hyping AI risk to lift stock prices or shut out rivals. Regulation, in his words, is "desperately needed".He admitted his exit will have a very small impact, "but not no impact; some of my skills are rare". The timing, he said, has nothing to do with the recent wave of viral resignations. He had picked the date long ago, ahead of a ten-day backpacking trip with friends on New Zealand's Abel Tasman and Wangapeka tracks.He is not walking away from AI altogether. O'Callahan will keep maintaining the debugging tools rr and Pernosco, and plans to study how AI agents debug code. He wants his next project to be "unambiguously pro-human".
Article Summary: Robert O'Callahan, a Google DeepMind engineer based in Auckland, has resigned over how fast artificial intelligence is advancing. In a resignation email shared on his blog this week, he wrote that AI progress is "far too rapid" His team's goal of making AI "much cheaper and lower-latency", he added, was not good for people right now. But he stops short of the extinction warnings that have dominated the AI debate.

Article Title: Microsoft launches new Copilot with AI agents, Office tools and a new Code feature: Here’s everything you need to know
Article Text:
Microsoft Copilot gets a new Home experience

Code lets users build apps and workflows

Autopilot can continue working on tasks

More business data and plugins

Microsoft updates Copilot AI spending controls

Microsoft has introduced a new version of Copilot. The latest version brings AI agents, Office tools and a new Code feature into a single experience. The tech giant is positioning the updated Copilot as a place where users can ask questions, delegate longer tasks, create documents and build small software solutions.The update adds three key capabilities: Home, Code and Autopilot. Home brings Chat and Cowork together, Office in Copilot adds Word, Excel and PowerPoint capabilities, while Code lets users create apps, dashboards and workflows using natural-language instructions. Meanwhile, Autopilot is designed to continue working on assigned tasks without requiring a new prompt each time.Microsoft has confirmed that Home will become Copilot's starting point, combining Chat and Cowork in one interface. Chat is designed for questions, lookups, and drafting, while Cowork handles multi-step tasks and produces a completed result.Microsoft said Copilot will eventually be able to determine whether a request should be handled by Chat, Cowork or Code, removing the need for users to select a mode themselves.The company is also bringing Office capabilities directly into Copilot. Users will be able to create or update Word documents, Excel workbooks and PowerPoint presentations from the Copilot interface.Files remain editable and can stay synchronised with the corresponding Microsoft 365 applications.The new Code feature aims to let non-developers create small, purpose-built software solutions. Users can describe an app, tracker, dashboard, automation or workflow in natural language, after which Copilot builds it.Microsoft said Code uses the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot and operates in a sandboxed environment. Solutions can include desktop widgets, interactive dashboards and cloud-hosted internal applications.Code is scheduled to enter Microsoft's Frontier programme at the end of the month, with broader availability planned in the following weeks. A preview will also be available to Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro subscribers later this year.Microsoft is also introducing Copilot Managed Runtime, a hosting environment that lets applications created through Code, Cowork, and Copilot Studio run within an organisation's Microsoft 365 environment.Autopilot, previously known as Scout, is Microsoft's persistent agent designed to continue working after a user assigns it a goal. Users can give Autopilot a name, role and objective, after which it can monitor channels, follow up on conversations and handle recurring work. The agent operates in the cloud and has its own identity, memory, computer and workspace within the organisation's tenant.Microsoft said Autopilot is designed to work across Teams, Outlook, chats, channels and documents, while remaining subject to permissions, auditing and organisational controls. Autopilot will expand to private preview at the end of September.Microsoft is expanding Copilot's access to business context through Microsoft IQ. Fabric IQ brings data from Power BI semantic models into Copilot, while integration with Dynamics 365 and Power Platform is planned for public preview.A new plugin registry will also bring Microsoft, partner and custom-built plugins into one catalogue. Administrators can approve and manage plugins centrally.Microsoft is also adding FinOps capabilities for managing AI spending. The company is separating everyday Copilot use from longer-running agentic workloads.A user subscription license covers Copilot across applications such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams. Usage-based billing applies to features including Cowork, Code and Autopilot.New administrative controls will let organisations manage spending policies, model availability, and credit requests. Users will also be able to see their credit usage, remaining balances and usage history within Copilot.Home and Code will begin rolling out through Microsoft's Frontier programme, while Autopilot is moving to private preview. Microsoft said it will continue rolling out additional Copilot features over the coming months.
Article Summary: Home brings Chat and Cowork together, Office in Copilot adds Word, Excel and PowerPoint capabilities. Code lets users create apps, dashboards and workflows using natural-language instructions. Autopilot is designed to continue working on assigned tasks without requiring a new prompt each time.

Article Title: OpenAI's AI agents hacked Australian government health website; alert email sent a month later to Public mailbox; upset Australian PM says: I spoke with Sam Altman to tell ...
Article Text:
Representative Image. In pic: Sam Altman

“Today, I spoke with the CEO of OpenAI,

Sam Altman

, to express Australia's extreme concern about this incident. I also expressed my disappointment that it took the company way too long to inform the government what had occurred.”

What happened during the OpenAI AI test

“didn't accept no for an answer”

OpenAI found the breach in August

“During this review, we identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers and available statistics for questions about Australia during an internal evaluation,”

“In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend,”

Australian government was notified through public mailbox

Australia launches investigation

ChatGPT maker OpenAI 's AI agents hacked Australian government health website. The incident happened in June, when an OpenAI model being evaluated for training was asked to research Australian government spending on medicines. According to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, the AI agent initially encountered restrictions on an Australian Medicare statistics portal but found a way around them and accessed public and non-public files.The Australian government says there is no evidence that any personal Medicare data was accessed. There has also been no breach of government systems. However, this issue has raised questions about how easily AI systems can bypass security measures. It has also raised questions about how long it takes for OpenAI to contact the authorities.According to a report by AFP, Albanese said,He added that the notification was also unacceptable because it was sent to a public mailbox rather than directly to the relevant government officials.The incident took place on June 18 while OpenAI was conducting internal evaluations of its AI models. Government Services Minister Katy Gallagher said the model had been asked to search for information about Australian government spending on medicines.The AI agent interacted with several government websites. On the Medicare statistics portal, it encountered restrictions but continued attempting to obtain information. Albanese described the model as havingand finding a way around the blocks.The accessed material included non-public aggregate health statistics and internal file names. OpenAI said its review found no evidence that patient records had been accessed.OpenAI did not identify the activity immediately. According to the Australian government, the company discovered the incident on August 11 while reviewing potentially misaligned model activity during training.OpenAI said it was conducting an extensive review of its models when it identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services. The company said its models were attempting to find answers and statistics about Australia during an internal evaluation.OpenAI said.the company added.Although OpenAI identified the incident in August, Australian authorities were not notified until September 10, almost a month later. The notification was sent to a public Services Australia mailbox that is used for reports from academics and researchers.Gallagher said the mailbox is checked once a day and can receive multiple notifications, including hoaxes. Services Australia reviewed the message before reporting the incident to Australia's cyber security agency on September 15.The timeline has become a major concern for the government. Albanese said the delay in reporting the incident was unacceptable, while OpenAI has said it is providing technical information to assist the investigation.Australia has launched a rapid review of the incident involving the prime minister's department, the Australian Signals Directorate and the country's AI Safety Institute. The review will examine what happened and whether existing rules adequately cover incidents involving autonomous AI systems.Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles compared the incident to an AI system “scaling the fence” after being denied access. He said the breach was serious but that no personal information had been accessed.The incident comes as concerns grow over AI models interacting with real-world computer systems. OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported instances in which models gained unauthorised access during testing, while Google has also disclosed security-related activity involving its AI systems.OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was in New York for discussions on AI risks at the United Nations when the Australian government made the incident public. Albanese said he had spoken directly with Altman about Australia's concerns and the delay in notification.
Article Summary: ChatGPT maker OpenAI's AI agents hacked Australian government health website. The incident happened in June, when an OpenAI model was asked to research Australian government spending on medicines. The AI agent initially encountered restrictions on an Australian Medicare statistics portal but found a way around them.

Article Title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber is its fourth cybersecurity model this year, here's what's coming
Article Text:
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: Timing amid growing AI security concerns

Part of a bigger DevDay push

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is preparing to unveil its latest cybersecurity-focused model named GPT-6 Cyber. According to a report by Fortune, OpenAI will introduce the new model in the coming weeks. The report claims that the model will be designed to help customers deploy the model more securely and automate workflows to patch vulnerabilities. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks. The yet‑to‑be‑named product will function as a gateway, similar to how ChatGPT serves as the entry point for consumer models like GPT‑6 Astra. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. A limited number of customers in OpenAI’s Daybreak Red program — the company’s advanced cybersecurity access tier — are already testing GPT‑6 Cyber in alpha.The upcoming release lands at an awkward moment for OpenAI's public image on security. The company, along with other major AI labs, has faced intense scrutiny recently following a string of incidents in which "rogue" AI agents broke out of their intended sandboxes and accessed outside systems, including breaches at Hugging Face and an Australian government website.Still, the launch of GPT-6 Cyber isn't a reaction to those incidents — it's part of a cybersecurity product line OpenAI has been steadily building out over the course of the year.GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026 alone, following GPT-5.4 Cyber in April, GPT-5.5 Cyber in June, and GPT-5.6 Cyber in August. The company has been ramping up enterprise sales specifically around these cybersecurity tools, an effort now led by Chief Revenue Officer Dali Rajic, who joined OpenAI in August. Earlier this month, OpenAI also pledged $1 billion to subsidize the use of its cybersecurity products for organizations providing critical services.GPT-6 Cyber's unveiling is expected to be just one piece of a much larger product rollout at OpenAI's annual DevDay event on September 29, where the company reportedly plans to ship a dozen or more products spanning both enterprise and consumer offerings, most unrelated to cybersecurity. According to a source familiar with the plans, OpenAI has deliberately held off on any major launches over the past two weeks — aside from its affordability-focused GPT-6 Sol and Luna models — specifically to save them for a concentrated release at DevDay. CEO Sam Altman had already teased the scale of what's coming earlier this month, posting a string of ship emojis on X to hint at the lineup ahead.

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

“Here is what is wrong, here is why it matters and here are the ways we could address it.”

We all come across problems that can feel too complicated, distant or difficult to solve. Whether it is a challenge at work, a business problem, or a larger issue affecting society, simply pointing out that something is wrong doesn't always lead to action. People are more likely to respond when they understand both the problem and what can be done about it.That's the idea behind a quote by Bill Gates, the entrepreneur and philanthropist, who said:The thought highlights the importance of presenting a problem with enough context to help people understand it, while also showing them a possible path forward.Gates' statement is closely connected to framing a problem. A problem can look very different depending on how it is presented, just like a picture can look different depending on how it is framed.Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly. It also puts boundaries around the problem, making it easier to examine rather than treating it as one large, undefined issue.But framing is not only about identifying what is wrong. It is also about putting the problem into context and showing people their options.For example, instead of simply saying a business is losing customers, a better approach is to look at who those customers are, what they need, what is changing in the market, and what competitors are doing differently.Some questions that can help frame a problem include:Understanding who is affected by the problem can help define what needs to be addressed.Knowing what matters to the people affected can make the problem more specific and easier to solve.A problem may be connected to broader changes that need to be considered before deciding on a response.Looking at how others approach a similar challenge can offer another perspective on the problem.Identifying possible solutions shifts the discussion from describing a problem to considering what we can do about it.Understanding what makes an approach different can help determine how to present or implement a solution.Technology can change both the nature of a problem and the solutions available to address it.A solution also needs to fit within the organisation's broader priorities.It is easy to tell people that something needs to change. It is much harder to get them to understand why it matters and what they can actually do about it.That is where framing becomes important. A problem presented without context can feel overwhelming or irrelevant. But when people can see the problem clearly and understand the possible solutions, they have a better basis for deciding how to respond.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, saying that a project is falling behind may not be enough to get people moving. Explaining what is causing the delay, who is affected and what options are available gives the team a clearer picture of the situation.The idea also changes the way we communicate problems. Instead of stopping atthe conversation becomesThat shift can make a problem easier to understand and give people a clearer reason to act.
Article Summary: Bill Gates said: “I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly.

Article Title: Inside Amazon India’s playbook for the Great Indian Festival 2026
Article Text:
Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

In a conversation with The Times of India, Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at

Amazon India

"To make our delivery experience more integrated and seamless, we have our Unified Delivery Service across over 300 cities, alongside, we have recently introduced Open Box Delivery on eligible high-value products will allow customers to verify the product at the time of delivery before accepting it. Together, these offerings bring greater choice, value, discovery and convenience to customers this festive season." Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India

‘Rising component costs has not dented premium ambitions’

‘AI popularity moves beyond smartphones’

Amazon Great India Festival dates

India’s consumer electronics landscape is seemingly seeing a decisive shift. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions. As households gear up for the festive season, shoppers are demanding premium hardware, tangible artificial intelligence capabilities, and transparent value., spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country, drawing insights from the platform’s 'Best in Tech' Survey."As customers become more deliberate and research-led in their technology purchases, the Best in Tech Survey was conducted to understand the features, innovations and value propositions that matter most to them across categories," Khan explained. The survey, based on 40,000-plus responses across primary consumer electronics categories, revealed that consumer priorities have fractured into distinct, highly specialized buckets.In the smartphone arena, the baseline expectations, as per Amazon survey, remain rooted in speed and battery stamina, with raw performance leading the pack. Yet, emerging software capabilities are swiftly ascending the priority list.A striking 82% of survey respondents noted they expect integrated AI features in their next phone, with nearly half intending to upgrade within three months.A parallel evolution is taking place in personal computing. Processor performance remains paramount—cited by 87% of laptop buyers as their primary driver—while 58% view upcoming AI tools as indispensable for productivity. Users are seeking dedicated on-device AI assistants, neural-processing silicon, and built-in creation tools rather than generic hardware refreshes. Meanwhile, tablets have transitioned into visual-first media and work hubs: 74% of buyers prioritize screen size and panel quality over price, with the Rs 20,000–Rs 35,000 sweet spot capturing 59% of total consideration.The electronics industry has weathered consecutive waves of inflationary pressure driven by surging memory and chipset costs. Yet, rather than trading down to cheaper alternatives, Indian consumers are exercising patience. "There is no doubt that prices are rising and customers have seen several rounds of pricing increases due to higher chip and memory costs. At the same time, we are seeing a lot of pent-up demand, with customers holding on to their upgrades rather than compromising on what they want. Premiumisation is not going away," said Khan.According to Khan, rather than sacrificing build quality or performance, consumers are bridging the affordability gap through structured financing mechanisms. Exchange schemes, bank tie-ups, instant credit via Amazon Pay, and No-Cost EMI plans have evolved into essential purchasing levers. For large appliances, 47% of consumers identify No-Cost EMI as their single most critical pricing enabler."Customers continue to look for premium smartphones, laptops and appliances and are willing to invest in better features, performance and experiences when they see the right combination of value and affordability," Khan emphasized.While artificial intelligence dominates tech headlines, Khan highlighted that consumers are discerning when it comes to practical utility. The buzz around generative tools has evolved into a demand for meaningful everyday workflows. "We are seeing growing interest in AI across categories. Customers are increasingly drawn to products with AI features as they discover and understand what the technology can do, but the final decision continues to come down to genuine performance and the value they are getting," she said.Importantly, Khan noted that beyond smartphones, interest in AI extends to laptops, where AI capabilities are increasingly becoming part of the upgrade cycle; and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances, where AI-enabled features are becoming part of the consideration. The broader trend is towards customers looking for technology that is relevant to their specific use cases, whether that is gaming, creation, work or everyday use. She said, "It definitely extends beyond smartphones. On smartphones, AI features are becoming increasingly important as customers discover and understand what the technology can do, but they continue to evaluate the device on fundamentals such as camera, processing speed and everyday performance. Beyond smartphones, we are seeing this interest extend to laptops... and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances."Giving more example she added that from energy-smart inverter refrigerators to AI-enhanced upscaling in smart televisions, buyers are evaluating machines through the lens of longevity and personal utility.To meet increase in demand as it heads into the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, the e-commerce giant is overhauling both discovery and post-purchase fulfillment. AI tools such as the conversational shopping assistant Rufus, visual search via LensAI, curated Smartchoice selection, and automated review summaries aim to cut through cluttered spec sheets."This festive season, we are focused on making product discovery easier and helping customers make more confident decisions," Khan noted, pointing out that peace of mind extends all the way to the doorstep. "Customers can benefit from open-box delivery on eligible products, giving them the opportunity to verify the product at the time of delivery. Our installation services are available across over 300 cities, helping customers get their appliances set up conveniently after purchase. "Amazon Great Indian Festival starts on October 8, 2026. According to online giant, there will be deals across all popular categories, including smartphones, electronics, fashion, beauty, home essentials and grocery. Customers also get a 10% instant discount on SBI Credit and Debit Cards and EMI transactions, and up to 10% extra only for Prime members.
Article Summary: Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions.

Article Title: 93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study
Article Text:
93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study

Key findings from the study

Google has released a study on the “Automobile Purchase Journey in the Age of AI”, highlighting how AI and digital surfaces are reshaping how India buys cars. According to the study, 93% of shoppers actively turn to AI during their research phase. Within this landscape, Google Search AI experiences play a critical role in evaluating complex specifications and financing. Consumers using AI actively navigate an average of 7.8 touchpoints to research and validate choices, reflecting a deeply considered, non-linear purchase journey, the study says.The study reveals that 87% of car buyers engage with Google platforms—including Search, YouTube, Maps, and Gemini—with Google Search widely cited by respondents as a key destination in the active research phase.Commenting on the evolving consumer journey, Siddharth Shekhar, Director, Google India, said, “The car buying journey in India is deliberate, non-linear, and deeply digital—particularly ahead of the festive season, when consideration peaks. Buyers move between discovery on YouTube and conversational validation on Search. Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% AI chatbots’ refers to conversational AI assistants such as Gemini and others.‘AI surfaces’ is a broader term encompassing these conversational assistants as well as generative AI experiences in Google Search that is AI Overviews and AI Mode. use AI Mode to navigate nuanced, complex queries. As AI helps buyers navigate complex choices, our ad and commerce solutions help automotive brands respond to their intent—connecting initial curiosity directly to the showroom.”Indian car buyers view their vehicle as a fundamental visual representation of personal achievement and lifestyle. However, final vehicle selection has decisively shifted toward a collaborative household effort, with 64% of consumers involving the whole family and 53% deciding alongside spouses.Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% leverage AI Mode for nuanced, conversational queries. Conversational AI triggers deeper validation: 80% of surveyed car buyers who use AI chatbots also turn to Google Search and/or YouTube during active research.YouTube functions as an always-on virtual showroom, where ~6 in 10 car buyers casually explore brands well ahead of their purchase decision. Through personalized Home Feeds, lifestyle vlogs, and creator content, passive discovery evolves into active consideration, anchored by 77% of YouTube users who rely on professional reviewers for trusted advice.AI acts as an expansionary force in active researchVirat Khullar, Head – Marketing, Hyundai Motor India Limited said,"The automotive purchase journey is increasingly shaped by moments of discovery, research and intent across digital channels. Our partnership with Google helped us harness the scale of YouTube to build awareness and the intelligence of AI-powered Search ad solutions to identify and convert high-intent consumers. By unifying upper- and lower-funnel marketing, we were able to deliver a more relevant and efficient customer experience, turning consideration into action and driving strong sales momentum for Hyundai VERNA. "
Article Summary: 93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study. Consumers using AI actively navigate an average of 7.8 touchpoints to research and validate choices. Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% AI chatbots.
